label: SCG I.22 contingent conjunction: precise typed reply and D-to-E boundary
summary: Bounded investigation for #1595 and #319 of SCG I.22 nn.2–4, with public Latin n.2 dependency trilemma, n.3's direct objection (necessary esse and contingent conjunction), and n.4's two-case reply. First case: if the esse can be understood without the proposed essence, that essence is accidental relative to the esse and not the quiddity of the first necessary being which is the esse. Second written case (si autem non potest intelligi illud esse sine illa essentia, tunc illud esse absolute dependet ab eo a quo dependet coniunctio sua ad essentiam illam; et sic redit idem quod prius): if it cannot, the esse depends absolutely on whatever its conjunction depends on and the n.2 horns return. CORRECTION (owner source-fidelity finding and semantic challenge on PR #1602): the first draft wrongly called this second case an unwritten analyst completion; it is written in n.4 (la.wikisource oldid 132346; Corpus Thomisticum scg1014 §23713). Only the first case is formalized here; the second is not yet formalized, attribution deferred. n.3's 'non per se necesse' is formalized only by a modal proxy; a sibling dependence sense (per se = without a cause of necessity; dependet quantum ad coniunctionem) is recorded in definition b18c2550 and the note, not yet formalized, and every 'outside the reply' scope claim is relative to the modal proxy. No chapter-specific corpus source passage was materialized, so no new source claim or attributed definition was registered. The analyst profile in TruthCore/Latin/Aquinas/SummaContraGentiles/BookI/Chapter22Conjunction.lean reuses the q.3 a.4 Profile for the same x/esse/essence representation but keeps existence of an esse, its world-relative conjunction to a proposed quiddity, conceivability apart, accidentality to esse, identification of the first bearer with that esse, and genuine quiddity distinct. A structural derivation says necessary e with contingent e-q conjunction yields an accessible world where e still exists but e-q does not. The reply then applies three separately OPEN premises: world separation indicates intelligibility apart (analyst), intelligibility apart makes q accidental to e (source-orientation reading), and a q accidental to e is not the quiddity of x IDENTIFIED with e (source-orientation reading). This second result is explicitly marked an assembly/transcription, not independent premise warrant or essence–esse identity. Seven finite interpretations supply a positive contingent adjunct, independent omission controls for the three interpretation bridges, identification and esse necessity, and a stable necessary e-q union of distinct principles with q genuine quiddity. The direct D-to-E boundary control reuses NecessaryAt, NoExistingSupportAt and ActualUnderivedEssenceIdentity on one actual and necessarily existing underived bearer: represented esse and essence remain distinct while the first-case bridge bundle holds, since the union never separates. The bare D → E non-entailment was already witnessed by the existing TruthCore.Causality.UnderivedEssenceEsse.Controls (third conjunct, model varying); the new control adds only compatibility with the first-case bundle, and its empty support relation does not mention the conjunction, so it does not represent an uncaused union. It is not a model of the whole n.3–4 reply: n.4's second case, n.2 coverage and n.6 union causation are not encoded. 'Same esse' in the separation theorem is a structural surrogate (bearer existence, q.3 actuality and q's existence at the counterworld are not tracked). Exact reading, source limits, independent mechanism and reopening test are in docs/notes/scg-i22-contingent-conjunction.md. This branch adds no root edge or closure marking; root premise change none. Kernel, binding, Comparator and NanoDa checks run in CI on PR #1602.
blocker: The formalized first n.4 case excludes one contingent essence-esse attachment only when the bearer is ontically identified with its esse and the three interpretive bridges hold. The stable distinct union survives the first case, relative to the modal proxy; a co-fundamental union must still answer n.4's second written case (by having no conjunction source), n.2's consonance trilemma (needs coverage) and n.6's union causation (quae per se non sunt unum, si coniungantur, oportet per aliquam causam uniri). D→E otherwise requires those premises or q.3's efficient-causal premises. Next slice: formalize n.4's second case as an explicit OPEN premise with OPEN semantics for intelligibility, the conjunction's source (conjunctionDependsOn) and per se underived necessity (with n.2's clause per se necessary e → no s on which e absolutely depends), with controls (a) conjunction dependent on q, expected refuted via n.2 horn (i), and (b) co-fundamental union with empty conjunction source, expected to survive and pass to n.2 coverage and n.6. Then type the three n.2 dependence directions using distinct relata and test coverage, actual underivedness, and the essence-as-accident conclusion against the stable distinct-union model; search for positive, independently defended co-fundamentality before treating that model as a substantive metaphysical rival. Then materialize/read a pinned SCG I.22 corpus passage before any source claim.
